blocks.text: Isothermal process constant temperature par hota hai, is liye gas par Boyle's law lagu hota hai. Yani gas isothermal tareeqe se phaile ya dabe to process ke dauran us ke pressure aur volume ka product (zarb ka jawab) constant rehta hai. Agar P₁, V₁ shuru ka pressure aur volume hon aur P₂, V₂ isothermal change ke baad ke (Fig. 6.7-a), to
Ideal gas ke molecules ki P.E. zero hai, is liye ideal gas ki internal energy sirf temperature par depend karti hai. Yahan temperature constant hai, is liye ΔU = 0, aur pehla law ban jata hai:

blocks.text: Yani agar gas phail kar bahar work W kare, to isothermal rehne ke liye use utni hi heat Q deni parti hai. Heat ko ek jagah se doosri jagah jane mein waqt lagta hai, is liye temperature constant rakhne ke liye expansion ya compression aahista hona chahiye. Isothermal process ko dikhane wala curve isotherm kehlata hai (Fig. 6.7-a).

blocks.prompt: Brain Teaser: isothermal expansion mein ideal gas ki internal energy constant kyun rehti hai?
blocks.explanation: Ideal gas ke molecules ki potential energy zero hai, is liye us ki internal energy sirf temperature par depend karti hai. Isothermal expansion mein temperature constant rehta hai, is liye ΔU = 0; gas jo work karti hai woh bahar se milne wali heat se poora hota hai (Q = W).
